text:
Camille: heads up — on a long-chat workload we've been seeing KV cache resident memory steadily grow over 2+ hours even when throughput is steady. eviction counters tick but reuse rates are down. i put a quick chart in the dashboard: https://grafana/redwood/d/kv-longcontext

Derek: :eyes: can you paste the prom queries you used? curious which metric is moving — residency% or live_pages

Camille: prom queries: 
- residency: sum(redwood_kv_resident_pages) / sum(redwood_kv_total_pages)
- reuse-rate: rate(redwood_kv_page_reuse_total[5m]) / rate(redwood_kv_page_loads_total[5m])
- evictions: rate(redwood_kv_evictions_total[1m])
(also a bucketed histogram for eviction_age_seconds)

Sanjay: nice. do we have per-model residency percentiles? overall % can hide hot-models hogging pages. would like p50/p95 residency by model_id label.

Camille: not right now — that's one of the gaps. dashboard shows global residency and an evictions timeseries. p95 would help.

Marta: what does the profiler say? any fragmentation metrics or unusually long-living fragments?

perf-bot: profiling summary (captured 2876543305): 
- top allocation sites: KVPage::alloc (45%), KVPage::append (20%)
- average fragment size increased from 4k -> 6.8k over 90m
- resident_pages growth correlated with sessions > 5k tokens
- cheap snapshot: no spikes in GC; memory growth is native heap, not JS/py heap

Derek: that suggests page chaining / coalescence issues when contexts get long. we've seen append-heavy workloads produce many small fragments that resist reuse.

Sanjay: suggestion: add a "fragmentation_ratio" metric: sum(fragment_free_bytes)/sum(fragment_total_bytes) per shard. also surface avg_fragment_age.

Camille: +1. also we should expose eviction_age_seconds histogram so we can tell whether we are evicting very young pages (inefficient) vs old pages. current counter only says count.

Marta: from an alerting POV i'd like two alerts: 
- residency_p95 > 80% for 10m (warn)
- evictions_per_min > 1000 && reuse_rate < 0.1 (sev)
these are heuristics, open to tuning.

Derek: adding to that — track live_pages vs active_pages. active_pages = pages referenced in last 15m. if live >> active then fragmentation or leak.

Camille: here's a quick prometheus patch i was going to try (pseudo):
```
# expose eviction age histogram
histogram_vec = prometheus.HistogramVec({
  name: "redwood_kv_eviction_age_seconds",
  buckets: [1,5,10,30,60,300,900,3600]
}, labels=["shard","model_id","reason"])

# increment on eviction
redwood_kv_eviction_age_seconds.labels(shard, model, reason).observe(eviction_age_seconds)
```

Sanjay: looks good. also instrument per-shard live_page_count and page_fragment_ratio. scrub labels for high-card models (sample top-N).

perf-bot: quick anomaly signal: model_id=chat-x-long shows reuse_rate drop at 2876542800 and steady page_loads spike around 2876543000. correlates with session durations > 8k tokens.

Marta: do we have a repro? infra-bot, can we run a canary that replicates 8k+ token chats and capture KV traces?

infra-bot: scheduled workload canary: canary/kv-long-context-1 will run across 3 shards for 90m starting 2876544000. logs to s3://redwood-canaries/kv-longcontext/2876544. will attach a link when done.

Derek: while canary runs, let's add panels: 
- stacked area: live_pages (by shard) vs active_pages 
- heatmap: eviction_age_seconds histogram over time 
- table: top models by resident_pages and reuse_rate

Camille: i'm going to open a tiny PR to: 
1) add eviction_age_seconds histogram + live_page gauges 
2) add p95 residency per model (sampled) 
3) add a debug flag to turn on high-cardinality labels for one canary run only

Derek: please add unit tests for the histogram buckets and a small e2e in the smoke test. we burned time once on a bad bucket choice.

Sanjay: one more ask — emit a labeled counter redwood_kv_eviction_cause_total{cause="fragmentation"|"age"|"oom"} so we can split reasons in dashboards.

Camille: noted. i'll add cause labels and default cause mapping: age when age>threshold else fragmentation if fragment_ratio>0.6 else oom. we can refine later.

Marta: timeline? can we have a dashboard patch + prom metrics in the next day so canary can validate?

Camille: i'll aim to open the PR in ~3h. canary starts in ~700s from now, so tight but possible to land metrics only and toggle high-card labels after.

infra-bot: canary started early (manual): canary/kv-long-context-1 started at 2876543385 (overridden). capturing prom scrape at 15s intervals.

perf-bot: FYI i pushed a quick flamegraph of KVPage::append – looks like a linear scan in coalesce on large fragments. attaching gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/kv-append-flame-287654

Derek: ok that's actionable: optimize coalesce to prefer tail append when fragment_count below threshold; also add fast-path for >8k token append to pre-allocate larger pages.

Camille: thanks all — will post PR link when ready and update dashboard panels. please react on the grafana mockups in the PR. :thumbsup:

Marta: thanks — fingers crossed canary gives us clean signals.

perf-bot: (reminder) correlate with kernel selection and batching changes — a kernel that changed append behavior two releases ago might have affected fragment size distribution. check release 2026.01.

Derek: good call. i'll diff kernels between 2026.01 and 2026.03 particularly L2 cache-friendly alloc path.

Camille: final note: temporary mitigation idea — if reuse_rate < 0.05 for model_id sample, trigger aggressive coalescence sweep for that shard for 1 minute. could reduce live_pages quickly while we tune. open to objections.

Sanjay: sounds reasonable as a short-term mitigation. log actions to avoid flapping.

Camille: will add as an optional canary experiment flag.

infra-bot: canary logs available: s3://redwood-canaries/kv-longcontext/2876544/ (will take a few mins to finalize).

Derek: great thread — followups: PR review, dashboard panels, and kernel diff. i'll take kernel diff. Camille/Sanjay take metrics + dashboard. Marta owns alert tuning.

Camille: on it.
